transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Sana (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Marcus (Aurora CTO), Priya (Aurora ML), Daniel (Aurora DevOps), Aisha (Aurora PM)

Summary:
- Intro discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart, focused on time-to-first-token, free credits, and evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Aurora Tech's inference needs.
- Customer has latency-sensitive features and regulatory concerns (data residency for EU customers).
- Agreed next steps: send pricing, SOC2/compliance docs, provision trial account with credits, run technical benchmark.

Topics:
- Quickstart and free credits
- Time-to-first-token and SDKs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security/compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs)
- Benchmark plan and rollout timeline

Transcript:
00:00 Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on this account, with Sana and Liam from engineering. How's everyone do-
00:06 Marcus: Good, thanks. We got a few priorities to run through. We'll be short on time, hope that's okay.
00:12 Evan: Totally, we'll keep it focused. Could you kick off with a little context on what Aurora's building and the main evaluation criteria?
00:21 Marcus: Sure, quick background — we run a real-time recommendations service that needs sub-200ms p95 for generation. We're evaluating a few paths: hosted API for initial rollouts, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for data residency. Main things are latency, cost, and security (we have EU customers).
00:41 Priya: Also, we have ~100k monthly active users, spikey traffic, and want seamless SDKs for Node and Python. Time-to-first-token for devs matters a lot — we want engineers onboard in hours not days.
00:56 Sana: Great, that's exactly where Redwood's PLG quickstart is designed to help — low friction sign-up, free credits, and quick SDK examples get you to first token in under an hour for many teams. Do you have an SRE or infra lead owning deployments?
01:09 Daniel: Yeah I'll be owning the infra side. We use GCP and run Kubernetes. For Private we'd prefer VPC peering and customer-managed KMS if possible.
01:19 Evan: Noted. Quick clarifying question: do you expect to keep models in your VPC or use Redwood-hosted model catalog initially?
01:26 Marcus: Initially prefer Redwood-hosted models to move fast, but long-term we want ability to bring our own model artifacts and pin versions.
01:34 Evan: That's a common path — start hosted then migrate to Dedicated or Private when you need capacity and control.
01:39 01:40 Sana: Technical note — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private gives you the control for KMS and network isolation but takes a bit more setup.
01:48 Marcus: How long is that "bit more setup"? We want an estimate for Private deployment timeline.
01:53 Sana: Typical Private on VPC with our autopilot template is 3-6 weeks after sign-off — can be faster if you provide infra access and we run a co-managed deployment.
02:03 Marcus: That's helpful. And Dedicated?
02:06 Evan: Dedicated can be provisioned in days to a couple weeks depending on commit level and region capacity. You also get SLAs for uptime/latency.
02:14 Priya: On quickstart — what's included in the free credits and how do we measure time-to-first-token?
02:19 Evan: Free credits are applied to the hosted API to let you test generation, embeddings, and streaming. Time-to-first-token depends on your dev flow, but our quickstart guide + SDKs typically get you to first call in 15-45 mins if you have basic API key and network access. We'll send a step-by-step.
02:34 Priya: Are there sample apps or a Postman/Insomnia collection?
02:37 Liam: Yes, we have quickstart repos for Node/Python, plus a Postman collection and a small Next.js example. We'll link those in the trial invite.
02:44 Daniel: On networking: for hosted, are requests proxied through Redwood's control plane? Any egress concerns for EU traffic?
02:51 Sana: Hosted runs in regional clusters; you can pick EU regions to keep data in-region. For extra compliance you can choose Dedicated or Private where network is fully controlled. We also have options for logging and audit retention.
03:03 Aisha: What compliance certs do you have? SOC2? ISO?
03:06 Evan: We are SOC 2 Type II and have a compliance pack — we'll share a whitepaper and an excerpt of the SOC2 assertion. We also support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations.
03:18 Marcus: Good. One concern — vendor lock-in vs cost. How easy is it to switch models or stop using Redwood if performance or costs don't match?
03:27 Sana: We design for portability: standard model formats, ability to export logs/metrics, and we encourage canary and A/B rollouts. Cost levers are batching, quantization suggestions, and routing policies. We'll show a cost/perf playbook.
03:41 Marcus: For the benchmark, we want to test our prompt shape and sequence lengths — p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens. Can you run a bench on Redwood-hosted and a Dedicated config?
03:50 Sana: Yes, we can run hosted tests quickly with your sample workload. For Dedicated we'll provision a small pool and run the same workload. We'll need sample prompts, token sizes, and expected concurrency.
03:59 Marcus: Ok I'll share a dataset of ~500 sample prompts and expected concurrency profile.
04:04 Evan: Perfect. We'll add that as an action item.
04:06 04:10 Priya: Any gotchas with streaming responses? We rely on token-level latency for UI snappiness.
04:13 Liam: Streaming is supported for generation and chat. The runtime optimizes KV cache and continuous batching for lower tail latency; you can tune batching window to favor latency over throughput.
04:26 Daniel: For Private: do you support on-prem air-gapped installs?
04:29 Sana: Yes, we offer an on-prem package for highly regulated or air-gapped customers; it requires more validation but it's supported.
04:36 Marcus: Great. On pricing, what are typical unit costs for Hosted vs Dedicated? I know it varies by model/region but looking for a ballpark.
04:45 Evan: Ballpark for hosted is per-token pricing (model dependent). Dedicated is lower unit costs for a capacity commit; we can share a pricing sheet with example unit economics and estimated monthly spend for your projected usage.
04:55 Marcus: Send that, please.
04:57 Evan: Will do.
05:00 Aisha: Who would be our Redwood contact once we start a pilot?
05:04 Evan: I'll be AE, Sana will lead technical onboarding and run the bench with you. Liam will help with SDK and rapid POC.
05:12 Marcus: Ok timeline: we're aiming to decide vendor by end of month, pilot in early next month if options look good.
05:18 Evan: That's doable. We'll get trial details and SOC2 over today or tomorrow and propose benchmark slots for next week.
05:24 Priya: One more question — any limits on model catalog or bringing custom quantized models?
05:31 Sana: You can bring your own model artifacts; for quantized models we have guidance on supported formats and kernel selection. For production, we recommend testing fallback variants as well.
05:41 Marcus: Sounds good.
05:45 Evan: Recap quick: 1) Evan to send pricing and trial invite with free credits, quickstart links. 2) Sana to prepare benchmark plan and Dedicated/Private checklist. 3) Marcus to share sample prompts and concurrency. 4) Schedule bench next week. We'll also share compliance docs. Anything to add?
06:05 Marcus: That's it. Thanks, talk soon.
06:08 Evan: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
